clue.text: Lacking a full complement, subordinate developed fast and provided input

parts.note: a subordinate is under someone, so the word gives UNDER

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: to provide input is to feed, past tense fed

explanation.surface: A thinly staffed office where a junior worker rose quickly and chipped in ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of 'fast'; the surface reads 'fast' as speed, but it is only anagram material here.
explanation.definitionFit: An organisation without enough workers to fill every post is short-handed, missing part of its complement.

clue.text: Numbers at wit's end with curious cure

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from wit

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
rum is an old British word for odd or curious

explanation.surface: A strange remedy offered in quantity by someone at the limit of their patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at wit's end' gives the last letter of WIT, T. RUM, meaning strange, is everyday British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, a supposed medicine of doubtful worth.

clue.text: Let spies deliver letters

indicators.note: to deliver is to set free, so the letters of the two words are released into a new order

explanation.surface: Spies are allowed to hand over their secret correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliver' rearranges LETSPIES; the surface makes 'letters' sound like post, but the definition means formal written epistles as in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistles are formal letters, especially those of the apostles in the Bible.

clue.text: Where tools may be kept or discarded

definitions.meaning: a small garden hut used for storing tools
to discard is to cast off, as a snake does its skin

explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut stores implements, and to cast off something is the verb of the same spelling, past tense.

clue.text: Enraged, a father left the city — city's most upset

parts.note: pop is an informal name for a father
EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upwards, so the piece reads in reverse
most of a word means all but its last letter, so the word city is cut short

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A father storms off, livid at what the capital has done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' trims CITY to CIT, which 'upset' turns to TIC. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone apoplectic is so furious they seem about to burst, overcome by rage.

clue.text: Brief indulgence in Scottish dance

definitions.meaning: a short spell of pleasure or a passing romance
the Highland reel danced solo in Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived affair or spree is one sense; the other is the lively Highland dance of Scotland.

clue.text: I reach a conclusion about the killer of a god

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for reaching a conclusion is placed around the letter I

parts.note: to reach a conclusion is to decide

explanation.surface: A detective works out who murdered a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Deicide, from Latin deus, names the slayer of a divine being as well as the act.

clue.text: Rock featuring ores bearing silver

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A geologist describes a rock with metal-bearing ores in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like a geological noun but is a verb that rearranges FEATURINGORES.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentiferous, from Latin argentum, describes ore or rock yielding the precious metal Ag.

clue.text: Chairman tried out — he's superior to Orthodox monks

indicators.note: out means wrong or misplaced, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chairman was given a trial run before the monastery took him on as its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An archimandrite is the head of a large monastery in the Eastern Church, ranking above abbots and ordinary brethren.

clue.text: Note bitchiness in the intermission

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
spite is malicious ill-feeling

explanation.surface: Catty remarks are passed in the theatre interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or pause, a lull between spells of activity.

clue.text: Man of the theatre finding source of oil right outside holiday centre

indicators.note: outside means the fruit's letters wrap around the following piece

parts.note: the olive is the fruit pressed for olive oil

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, here from holiday

explanation.surface: An actor drills for oil near a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of oil' looks like O, the first letter of oil, but it is OLIVE, which goes 'outside' I, the centre of 'holiday'.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was the leading English stage actor and director of the twentieth century.

clue.text: A bird regrets losing its wings

indicators.note: a word's wings are its first and last letters, so dropping them leaves its middle

explanation.surface: A bird regrets that it can no longer fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing its wings' takes the first and last letters off 'regrets'.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron, a wading bird.

clue.text: Hit Lillian for being slow

parts.note: to slug is to punch hard
Lillian Gish was an American silent-film star

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a woman for dawdling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish means sluggardly and lacking energy, moving at a dull pace.

clue.text: Puppet — one with talking head -in degree ceremony

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the following pieces go within the word for ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from talking

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist's dummy is brought along to a graduation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking head' is the first letter of 'talking', not a TV pundit; 'in' places that and the word for one inside the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A marionette is a figure worked by strings, a kind of doll moved by a puppeteer.

clue.text: Teetotalism met setback peer can get smashed

indicators.note: setback read as set back turns the word met backwards
to get smashed is to be broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teetotal campaigner meets a lord whose tin of beer leaves him drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns MET to TEM; 'get smashed' rearranges PEERCAN to PERANCE. 'smashed' means drunk, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance is abstaining from alcohol, as in the nineteenth-century movement against drink.

clue.text: A supermodel's hairdo

indicators.note: the 's stands for has, so the word holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A fashion model's new hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A perm is a permanent wave, a styled curling of hair.

clue.text: From La Scala mariners bring seafood

indicators.note: from means taken out of, so the answer is lifted from within the words

explanation.surface: Sailors visiting the Milan opera house bring squid.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala is the Milan opera house; the run crosses 'Scala' and 'mariners'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid cooked as food.

clue.text: They serve senior pupils with cigarettes

definitions.meaning: in British boarding schools junior boys once acted as servants to older ones

explanation.definitionFit: Junior boys who ran errands for older ones at English public schools shared their name with slang for smokes.

clue.text: Information on Morecambe is not specific

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian

explanation.surface: Details about a seaside town are vague.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire seaside town, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe, half of Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, applying to a whole class rather than one particular case.

clue.text: Forecast share-out for cooperative people

parts.note: the divi was the dividend paid to members of a British Co-op store
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A cooperative society predicts how profits will be split among its members.
explanation.walkthrough: The Co-op is a British chain of member-owned shops whose profit share was called the divi.
explanation.definitionFit: Divination is foretelling the future, as by augury or omens.

clue.text: Asunder like Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn

definitions.text: like Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn
definitions.meaning: these characters appear in the novels of Mark Twain

explanation.definitionFit: Split in halves is the old sense; Mark Twain's characters are found in his books, in the writer's works.

clue.text: Luxuriant heather is persistently annoying

parts.note: rank means growing too thickly, as weeds do
ling is the common heather

explanation.surface: Overgrown heather on the moor keeps irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rankling causes lasting bitterness, festering in the mind.

clue.text: Rugby players with hair

definitions.meaning: the two second-row forwards in a rugby scrum

explanation.definitionFit: Second-row forwards in a rugby scrum, and tresses on the head.

clue.text: Story curtailed by a press lord

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper owner cuts a news report short.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astor family owned The Times and The Observer, making them newspaper barons.

clue.text: Deputy head, boxer and artist

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here from deputy

parts.note: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: A deputy headteacher, a fighter and a painter make an odd trio.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter.

clue.text: United right-back goes to authentic Dutch city

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: back means reversed, so the abbreviation is read the other way

parts.note: echt is a German word, used in English, meaning genuine

explanation.surface: A football club's right-back moves to a genuine Dutch side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-back' looks like a football position, but 'back' turns RT to TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Utrecht is a university city in the central Netherlands.

clue.text: Unwavering neoclassical architect with article on National Trust

parts.note: Robert Adam was the Scottish neoclassical architect
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A determined architect writes a piece about the heritage body.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that owns historic houses, several of them designed by Robert Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means firm and immovable in one's resolve.

clue.text: Beauty is their trade — no asceticism is involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Beauticians make it plain that self-denial plays no part in their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges NOASCETICISM; the definition stretches over the whole first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmeticians are make-up experts who sell or apply cosmetics professionally.
